# Psalm 48 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A song. A psalm of the descendants of Korah.

**2** How great is the LORD, how deserving of praise, in the city of our God, which sits on His holy mountain!

**3** It is high and magnificent — the whole earth rejoices to see it! Mount Zion, the holy mountain, is the city of the great King!

**4** God Himself is in Jerusalem's towers, revealing Himself as its defender.

**5** The kings of the earth joined forces and advanced against the city.

**6** But when they saw it, they were stunned; they were terrified and ran away.

**7** They were gripped with terror and seized with panic, like a woman in labor.

**8** You destroyed them like the mighty ships of Tarshish shattered by an east wind.

**9** We had heard of the city's glory, but now we have seen it ourselves — the city of the LORD of Heaven's Armies. It is the city of our God; He will make it safe forever. Pause and reflect.

**10** O God, we meditate on Your unfailing love as we worship in Your temple.

**11** As Your name deserves, O God, You will be praised to the ends of the earth. Your strong right hand is full of justice.

**12** Let the people on Mount Zion rejoice. Let all the towns of Judah be glad because of Your justice.

**13** Go, inspect the city of Jerusalem. Walk around and count the many towers.

**14** Take note of the fortified walls, and tour all the citadels, that you may describe them to future generations.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **48:9**: 'We had heard... now we have seen' — the transition from secondhand faith to firsthand experience. Report becomes reality.

— PNEUMA
